requirements: R1: Rewrite the Dockerfile to use a multi-stage build.
R2: Build the backend JAR using Maven (maven:3.9-eclipse-temurin-17 AS build).
R3: Build the Svelte frontend (npm ci && npm run build) inside the frontend/ directory.
R4: Copy the compiled frontend dist/ into src/main/resources/static before building the backend JAR.
R5: Use a lightweight runtime image (eclipse-temurin:21-jre-alpine) for the final stage and copy the built JAR into it.
R6: The docker compose up --build command must succeed on a fresh repository clone without manual pre-compilation.

slices.title: Implement multi-stage Dockerfile with frontend static generation
slices.jtbd: When implementing the multi-stage build for this epic, I want to compile both frontend and backend within the container, so that the application can be built from a fresh clone without manual local builds.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a fresh clone of the repository without a target directory
When a user runs docker compose up --build
Then the image should build successfully and start the application container
And opening http://localhost:8080/ should serve the real frontend UI
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Reduce local setup failure rate from 100% to 0% on fresh clones

slices.title: Verify standalone Docker build and static asset serving
slices.jtbd: When verifying the multi-stage build for this epic, I want to ensure that the container builds from scratch and serves the frontend, so that we prevent regressions where local artifacts are accidentally required.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a local environment with Docker
When the image is built using the provided Dockerfile without a target/ directory
Then the build process should successfully complete without finding missing JARs
And when the container is started, it should return a 200 OK and frontend HTML on the root path
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Reduce deployment regression rate from 10% to 0% by testing container build end-to-end
